main_text.p: potentia quævis prima, si debeat in actum produci. Ut in animali non tantum est prima potentia Videndi, proximè fluens ab anima sensitrice, quam retinet perpetuò, sed etiam est certa dispositio oculi, per quam alius alio clarius videt. Hæc potest amitti.
SingularisSingularis est orta ex temperamento singulorum individuorum, quo aliud alii naturæ dotibus antecellit.
Huc itaq; pertinent Virtutes & dotes Natu-ræ, Generositas scilicet & Nobilitas na-turæ, quatenus accipitur pro evidenti dispositione animi & corporis ad virtutem omnem.
Huc refertur Ingenium & εὐφυΐα[?] ad doctrinam facilè apprehendendam, & dijudicandam. Item Judicii nativa dexteritas: Robur item corporis nativum. Huc item referri possunt συργαὶ φυσικαί[?], &c.
main_text.head: CAPUT SEXTUM. DE QUALITATIBUS ACTU-ALIBUS, SENSIBILIBUS, TAC-TILIBUS, PRIMIS.
main_text.p: Qualitas actualisValitas actualis est, quæ actu afficere sensum apta est. Ideoq; sensibilis dici potest, quia sensu percipitur.

page.notes: The right margin has a clear note "Singularis" and a clear note "Qualitas actualis". Faint, mirrored marginal words such as "Primar", "Termin", "Calor" and "Calovis" are show-through from the other side and are left out. Faint ghost lines below the text rule are also show-through. The Greek in "Ingenium & ... ad doctrinam" is uncertain: it looks like εὐφυΐα, marked [?]. The Greek after "Huc item referri possunt" is hard to read and is marked [?]. The heading's hyphenated word "ACTU-ALIBUS" and "TAC-TILIBUS" keep the printed hyphens; the printed V is read as U by the spelling rule. The initial of "Valitas" sits in an ornamented block. The bottom catchword "Omne" appears as the last printed word below the text.
